name: Joefe B. Santarita
half: Joefe B. Santarita has advised 6 theses in this repository between 2020 and 2023. Their research supervision covers several sub-topics, including governance and public policy, which appears in 5 items, culture and identity, which appears in 2 items, teacher training, which appears in 2 items, management and leadership, which appears in 1 item, arts and creative practice, which appears in 1 item, and community development, which appears in 1 item. Their advised work includes a 2023 study on Philippine and Vietnam strategies in the South China Sea conflict management, focusing on management and leadership and governance and public policy. They also supervised a 2023 thesis regarding the relevance of Maligay to contemporary Tausug and Malay societies, involving culture and identity and governance and public policy. In 2022, they advised a thesis on glocalizing K-Pop through Pinoy Pop and Thai Pop music, covering culture and identity, governance and public policy, and arts and creative practice. Another 2022 thesis supervised by them investigated the mobility of Filipinos teaching English-mediated subjects in Cambodia, Myanmar, and Thailand, focusing on teacher training. In 2021, they advised a thesis on designing a social protection program for Filipino teachers in Indonesia and Vietnam, involving teacher training, governance and public policy, and community development. Finally, they supervised a 2020 thesis on treaty commitment preferences regarding the proposed ASEAN extradition, focusing on governance and public policy.

Their supervision patterns show a strong focus on governance and public policy. In 2023, they advised Rex Marion C. Laguerta on a thesis regarding management and leadership and governance and public policy, which investigated how Vietnam and the Philippines manage territorial claims amidst Chinese expansionism and Sino-American geopolitical competition. In the same year, they advised Cherry Mae L. Ladja on a thesis regarding culture and identity and governance and public policy, which investigated the cultural significance of Maligay, a traditional Tausug food cart, within wedding celebrations in Jolo, Sulu. In 2022, they advised a thesis regarding culture and identity, governance and public policy, and arts and creative practice, which investigated how contemporary pop music in the Philippines and Thailand utilizes the K-Pop idol formula to create unique local expressions of evolving cultural identities in the ASEAN. Also in 2022, they advised Desiree Claro-Azucena on a thesis regarding teacher training, which investigated the drivers behind the migration of Filipino educators to Cambodia, Myanmar, and Thailand. In 2021, they advised Carl Ivan B. Villanueva on a thesis regarding teacher training, governance and public policy, and community development, which investigated the lived experiences and challenges of Filipino educators working in Southeast Asia, specifically in Indonesia and Vietnam, to design a social protection program. In 2020, they advised Kieren Roevi A. Batiles on a thesis regarding governance and public policy, which investigated the variables influencing the Philippines' decision to commit to and ratify international agreements, specifically the proposed ASEAN extradition treaty. While they have no advisee listed for 2026, their latest advisee year in this repository is 2023. They have 0 articles of their own in this repository. Their strengths in supervision are evident in their work on governance and public policy, teacher training, and culture and identity. Their supervision includes studies on the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, and the Tausug and Malay societies. Their work involves qualitative studies and investigations into international agreements, migration, and cultural expressions within the ASEAN.

Joefe B. Santarita has advised 6 theses in this repository between 2020 and 2023. Their research focus and supervision patterns show a strong emphasis on governance and public policy, which appears in 5 of their advised items. Other sub-topics covered in their supervision include culture and identity, which appears in 2 items, and teacher training, which appears in 2 items. They have also supervised work related to management and leadership, arts and creative practice, and community development, each appearing in 1 item. Their supervision covers various regional contexts, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, and the Tausug and Malay societies.

The theses supervised by Joefe B. Santarita include a 2023 study on the comparative assessment of Philippine and Vietnam strategies in the South China Sea conflict management, which covers management and leadership and governance and public policy. Another 2023 thesis investigated the relevance of Maligay to contemporary Tausug and Malay societies, focusing on culture and identity and governance and public policy. In 2022, they supervised a thesis on glocalizing K-Pop, specifically Pinoy Pop and Thai Pop music as glocal expressions of evolving cultural identities in the ASEAN, which covers culture and identity, governance and public policy, and arts and creative practice. Also in 2022, they advised a thesis regarding the mobility of Filipinos teaching English-mediated subjects in the basic education institutions of Cambodia, Myanmar, and Thailand, which falls under teacher training. In 2021, they supervised a thesis on designing a social protection program for Filipino teachers in ASEAN countries, specifically the case of Indonesia and Vietnam, which covers teacher training, governance and public policy, and community development. Their earliest supervised thesis in this repository is from 2020, which examined treaty commitment preferences regarding the case of the Philippines on the proposed ASEAN extradition, focusing on governance and public policy.

Evidence regarding their specific research strengths is limited to the distribution of these sub-topics. Their supervision shows a consistent interest in governance and public policy across multiple years. They have supervised students working on diverse themes ranging from conflict management and territorial contestation to cultural traditions and teacher migration. While they have no articles of their own in this repository, they have been active in advising theses from 2020 to 2023. There is no advisee listed for the year 2026. Their work with students involves a variety of qualitative approaches, such as case studies and interpretative phenomenological analysis, as seen in the summaries of the theses they have supervised. Their supervision covers a wide range of topics within the ASEAN context, including identity, social protection, and international agreements.
